newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares surge to three-month high.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares surge to three-month high.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped 4.61 percent on Friday to end at levels not seen in over three months.
The SBI index ended out the week 9.6 percent and above 1,000 points for the first time since June 20, when it stood at 1,004.77.
Traders cautioned, however, that the market could fall prey to a bout of correction next week after the recent rapid and heady gains.
"Lek, which has propelled the whole market in the past two weeks, seems to be stabilising. As a consequence, the market could start consolidating," Vera Dolinar, a trader at bank A banka said.
Drug maker Lek's A issue has risen 36.5 percent since being listed two and a half weeks ago.
* The seven-share SBI index soared 44.41 points to 1,007.25.
* 17 shares rose and three fell, while four were untraded.
* Lek's issue A was most again the most heavily traded, easing 0.5 percent to 18,800 tolars on volume of 9,162 shares for total turnover of 171.1 million tolars.
* Construction company GPG was the top gainer, jumping 9.85 percent to 7,250 on volume of 30 shares for total turnover of 0.2 million tolars.
* Pharmaceutical trader Salus was the leading decliner, falling 3.34 percent to 12,750 tolars on volume of 190 shares for total turnover of 2.5 million tolars.

* Preferred shares of trader Kovinotehna, which today announced it swung into the black in the first half of 1996, rose 0.74 percent to 408 on volume of 1,070 shares for total turnover of 0.4 million tolars.
Kovinotehna's ordinary shares eased 0.5 percent to 397 on volume of 9,880 shares for total turnover of 3.9 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
